question: does any 80186 RAM cell advance at the DSP's codec sample rate, i.e. is DSP data 0399 mirrored host-side
method: repeated ATGLK2= page reads of the five pages that differ between the two live passes in courier-board-21210-ram-01, each stamped with a host monotonic clock; every 16-bit cell unwrapped and rate-fitted
finding: One monotone counter, at 0x012a, running at 200.00 Hz - the 5.000 ms firmware tick. No cell advances at an audio rate. The other 29 moving cells are non-monotone with few distinct values; their fitted rates are artefacts of unwrapping noise, not counters.
resolution: A sweep is about 1.3 s, in which a 7200 Hz 16-bit counter advances about 9,360 - well inside one wrap - so the scan could have resolved one had it existed.
limits: Covers the low 64 KiB only, and within it only the pages that moved between two passes 69 s apart; a counter that happened to read equal at both would not be in that set.
The relocated peripheral block at 0xff00 and the 0x10000..0x1ffff window were not scanned.
A rate fit says how fast a cell advances, not what drives it.

rejected_as_unwrap_artefact.why: monotone only after unwrapping; raw first and last are equal, so it oscillates rather than counts
